notes.text: The Mishnah names Akavya and sets out his ruling on wool from a blemished firstborn.
Bavli presentation of the Mishnah.
Akavya named in the laws of the appearance of lesions.
Akavya and the sages differ on the retained white hair.
Akavya and the sages dispute the green discharge.
Parallel dispute over the ban and the administration of the sotah water. This passage supplies the dispute, while the chronology is explicitly in Yuḥasin.
The passage quotes the denial of excommunication and superlative praise. Hillel appears soon afterward in a separate account of the crowded courtyard.
Yuḥasin explicitly places Akavya after Shemayah and Avtalyon, in the time of Hillel and Shammai.
Heilprin and Bartenura have humility and fear of sin. Pesaḥim instead reads wisdom and fear of sin. Berakhot adds purity.
Akavya teaches reflection on three things. Heilprin characterizes the teaching as humility.
The Mishnah names the office and explains the refusal to retract.
The deathbed exchange is in 5:7. Heilprin reads three, where the extant Mishnah reads four. The overlay records both numerals.
The father had received his view from many and the son had received that view from an individual. The Mishnah also says the son heard the competing opinion of the majority.
The reply about his son’s deeds is continuous with the deathbed exchange in 5:7.
Rashi reads the comparison as one about the woman and the administering sages. Set out the shared status without leaving the comparison’s antecedent ambiguous.
Rambam explicitly construes דוגמא as imitation sotah water. Heilprin supplies the contrast with basin water and the purpose of frightening her.
Both traditions remain attributed. The reported ban and death, and Rabbi Yehudah’s explicit alternative, appear consecutively.
Yuḥasin explicitly qualifies the event as a possible ban without death under the ban and refers to Sifrei. The printed OCR has noise in the surrounding words.
The direct Yuḥasin reads a reference to Sifrei but gives no section. The checked Sifrei loci do not establish this exact proposition. Rambam’s account supplies a separate parallel for the ban.
Gelilot Eretz Yisrael is the provisional abbreviation expansion. Secondary burial notices do not replace precise primary collation for the grouped burial and exact location.
